records.text: Paper card. System: wear‐resistant materials, including coatings, surface textures, and bulk materials with various compositions and microstructures. Processing: various techniques, including physical vapor deposition, chemical vapor deposition, laser processing, electro processing, mechanical processing, chemical processing, plasma processing, gas nitriding, and ion implantation. Test conditions: different wear conditions, including dry sliding, micro‐abrasion, and water lubrication, with various loads, sliding speeds, and temperatures. Findings: 1.753; 2.7; 3.0; 4.6; 42.3; 72; 80; 96; the wear resistance of materials can be improved by surface engineering and matrix strengthening; the hardness of coatings is strongly related to their compositions and microstructures; the wear resistance of bulk materials can be improved by controlling compositions, designing microstructures, and adding reinforcements. Mechanism: the wear resistance of materials is influenced by various mechanisms, including lattice distortion, grain size effect, precipitation effect, grain boundary effect, dislocation or twinning effect, and the formation of tribolayers. item.research_question: How do material properties such as hardness, stiffness, strength, and cyclic plasticity affect wear resistance?
item.material_system: Various materials including metals, ceramics, polymers, and composites
item.test_conditions: Different testing conditions including sliding speed, contact stress, and temperature
key_findings: Hardness is a significant parameter in determining wear resistance
Substrate stiffness plays different roles in surface wear resistance in macro- and nanoscale domains
The wear resistance of ceramic-ceramic, ceramic-metallic, and metallic-metallic tribological systems depends on the H/E ratio
The ratio of the maximum contact stress to yield strength is a potential coefficient to assess polymer wear resistance
The wear resistance of amorphous materials is affected by the elastic mismatch between the surface and substrate
item.mechanism: The authors explain that the wear resistance is influenced by the material's intrinsic properties, such as hardness, stiffness, strength, and cyclic plasticity, as well as the testing conditions
item.limitations: The authors mention that there is a lack of data on the assessment of wear resistance using critical intrinsic material properties other than hardness
item.future_work: The authors suggest that future research should focus on the large-scale elaboration of nanostructures or phase compositions, computational modeling, and the anti-wear assessment of AM materials
quotes: Hardness is widely accepted as a significant parameter in determining the wear resistance
The wear resistance of the bulk can be increased by controlling its hardness, fracture behavior, plasticity, and strength

records.text: Paper card. Question: How do material properties such as hardness, stiffness, strength, and cyclic plasticity affect wear resistance?. System: Various materials including metals, ceramics, polymers, and composites. Test conditions: Different testing conditions including sliding speed, contact stress, and temperature. Findings: Hardness is a significant parameter in determining wear resistance; Substrate stiffness plays different roles in surface wear resistance in macro- and nanoscale domains; The wear resistance of ceramic-ceramic, ceramic-metallic, and metallic-metallic tribological systems depends on the H/E ratio; The ratio of the maximum contact stress to yield strength is a potential coefficient to assess polymer wear resistance; The wear resistance of amorphous materials is affected by the elastic mismatch between the surface and substrate. Mechanism: The authors explain that the wear resistance is influenced by the material's intrinsic properties, such as hardness, stiffness, strength, and cyclic plasticity, as well as the testing conditions. Limitations: The authors mention that there is a lack of data on the assessment of wear resistance using critical intrinsic material properties other than hardness. Future work: The authors suggest that future research should focus on the large-scale elaboration of nanostructures or phase compositions, computational modeling, and the anti-wear assessment of AM materials. Quote: "Hardness is widely accepted as a significant parameter in determining the wear resistance"
